newsitem.title: USA: Lawmaker plans bill to privatize US bank fund.
newsitem.headline: Lawmaker plans bill to privatize US bank fund.

text.p: As the chairman of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corp delivered a strong defense of her agency's performance, congressional critics prepared a proposal to eliminate the government role in bank insurance.

Although no legislation is currently pending, one of the FDIC's long-time critics, Rep. Thomas Petri, will introduce a bill in this session to privatize the insurance fund, a staffer to the Wisconsin Republican said on Friday.

"Rep. Petri has in the past introduced a bill to shift federal deposit insurance and the safety and soundness function to the private sector," legislative assistant Richard Markowitz said. "He plans to reintroduce the bill."
Petri's office is still tinkering with the wording of the bill, Markowitz said. He declined to say when the measure would be reintroduced.
In the past, congress has rejected the measure but FDIC chairman Ricki Helfer appeared to be launching a preemptive strike on Friday in a speech to the Independent Bankers Association of America.
Private insurance plans "have difficulty handling failures in waves and, therefore, are not good at stemming panic or contagion and cannot assure stability," she said.
